name: Bleeding in Pregnancy
source_guidance: Adapted from WHO recommendations on antenatal care and on managing obstetric emergencies (haemorrhage, ectopic pregnancy, pre-eclampsia), and NHS guidance on bleeding in pregnancy.

questions.text: Is the bleeding heavy, soaking a pad in an hour or less, or is she passing large clots?
Has she fainted, or is she dizzy, very pale, or very weak?
Is there severe belly pain, or pain in the shoulder tip?
Is she having a fit, or a severe headache with blurred vision?
Is she in the second half of pregnancy (about 5 months or more) and having any bleeding?
Is there any bleeding or spotting earlier in pregnancy, even if light?
Is there fever or a bad-smelling discharge?

emergency: Call 112 now, or get to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.
Go to the nearest hospital with a maternity unit now.
Lie down on her left side while waiting for transport.
Bring the antenatal card or clinic book.
Do not put anything inside the vagina.
urgent: Go to a hospital or clinic with a maternity service today.
Use pads, not tampons, so the amount of bleeding can be checked.
Call 112 if bleeding becomes heavy or severe pain starts.
self_care: No bleeding or warning signs were reported.
Call back at once if there is any bleeding, severe pain, headache with blurred vision, or reduced baby movements.
